findings.claim: Third-quarter 2026 net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion (13% excluding a $0.9 billion foreign-exchange headwind), operating income rose to $28.1 billion at a record 13.9% margin from $17.4 billion, and net income was $20.7 billion, or $1.89 per diluted share, versus $21.2 billion, or $1.95, primarily because the year-ago quarter included $9.5 billion of pre-tax gains on the Anthropic investment.

AWS net sales rose 39.3% to $46.0 billion in the third quarter of 2026, which Amazon described as a $184 billion annualized revenue run rate and its fastest AWS growth in nearly five years, and AWS operating income rose to $17.8 billion from $11.4 billion.

North America segment sales grew 6% to $112.9 billion and International sales grew 5% to $43.1 billion (8% excluding foreign exchange), while North America operating income rose to $8.7 billion from $4.8 billion; Amazon said moving Prime Day into the second quarter for most large countries reduced reported third-quarter growth by about 400 basis points.

Amazon guided fourth-quarter 2026 net sales to $240.0 billion to $247.0 billion, or 12% to 16% growth, and operating income to $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion versus $25.0 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025, and said advertising revenue, up 12% excluding foreign exchange in the third quarter, should grow at a high-teens rate in the fourth quarter.

Trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow rose 29% to $168.3 billion, but free cash flow was an outflow of $42.4 billion versus an inflow of $14.8 billion a year earlier, because purchases of property and equipment, net of proceeds and incentives, increased $94.8 billion year over year for artificial-intelligence investment, and Amazon still expects about $220 billion of cash capital expenditures in 2026.

Cash capital expenditures were $75.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026 and $172.2 billion for the first nine months, versus $34.2 billion and $89.9 billion a year earlier, and the 10-Q says cash capital expenditures are expected to increase meaningfully again in 2027, with a secured supplier-financing facility of up to about $80 billion available to draw from the first quarter of 2027 through the third quarter of 2028.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Unrecognized performance obligations on customer contracts with original terms longer than one year were about $578 billion as of September 30, 2026, with a weighted-average remaining life of 6.1 years, and in the second quarter of 2026 AWS and Anthropic expanded an existing multi-year commitment by more than $100 billion over 10 years, including obligations tied to AWS chips.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The face value of long-term debt rose to $180.887 billion at September 30, 2026 from $68.836 billion at December 31, 2025, including $37 billion of notes issued in March 2026, $25 billion issued in July 2026, foreign-currency notes in euros, Swiss francs, Canadian dollars and sterling, and a $17.5 billion term loan drawn in September 2026 that matures in September 2029.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: At September 30, 2026 Amazon held $55.783 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $58.443 billion of marketable securities, had no commercial paper outstanding and no borrowings on $20 billion of revolving credit facilities, and in October 2026 replaced those facilities with a $5 billion 364-day revolver maturing in October 2027 and a $15 billion revolver extending to October 2031.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: In the nine months ended September 30, 2026 Amazon recorded about $62.8 billion of upward Level 3 fair-value adjustments on Anthropic nonvoting preferred stock, and it agreed to a financing facility of up to $20 billion that had nothing available to draw at inception and becomes available only as AWS compute-delivery milestones are met, with draws taken in new Anthropic notes or, after a liquidity event, stock.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: As of September 30, 2026 Amazon carried Anthropic nonvoting preferred stock at $92.5 billion (164 million shares) and convertible notes at an estimated fair value of $146.2 billion, up from $14.8 billion and $45.8 billion at December 31, 2025, and those notes are subject to a 12% ownership cap that Amazon may waive.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: In August 2026 the FTC and 22 state attorneys general sued Amazon in the Western District of Washington, and Texas sued separately, alleging Amazon harmed advertisers through misrepresentations and unfair practices involving reserve prices in sponsored-ad auctions and seeking injunctions, civil penalties, restitution and disgorgement, which Amazon disputes.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Amazon's 10-Q describes antitrust cases pending since March 2020 in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom that seek billions of dollars of damages and structural relief, with one U.S. class action certified and three U.K. class actions certified.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: In June 2026 the U.S. International Trade Commission instituted an investigation of a Xockets complaint alleging that AWS EC2 P6e-GB200 UltraServers and related products infringe patents and seeking injunctive relief, and Xockets has also alleged infringement by AWS products with GB300 servers, which Amazon disputes.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Amazon granted 112.8 million restricted stock units in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, shares outstanding rose from 10.731 billion at December 31, 2025 to 10.811 billion at September 30, 2026, and it repurchased no common stock in the first nine months of 2025 or 2026, leaving $6.1 billion of the March 2022 $10 billion repurchase authorization unused.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On April 13, 2026 Amazon agreed to acquire Globalstar for cash of $90.00 per share or 0.3210 Amazon shares (value capped at $90.00), with cash elections capped at 40% of Globalstar shares, at an implied value of about $10.9 billion including debt, with closing expected in 2027 subject to regulatory approvals and satellite-replacement milestones.
findings.source_title: Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Amazon said it would invest more than $1.5 billion to raise the minimum starting pay for U.S. full-time operations employees to $20 an hour and to add a grocery discount and a lifetime banking benefit.

Amazon's fourth-quarter outlook says results may be materially affected by tariff and trade policies and by resource and supply volatility, including for memory chips, and the guidance assumes that no additional legal settlements are concluded.

upcoming_catalysts.event: Fourth-quarter 2026 results versus guided net sales of $240.0-$247.0 billion and operating income of $28.5-$33.5 billion
Secured supplier-financing facility of up to about $80 billion becomes available for technology-infrastructure purchases
Expected close of the Globalstar acquisition, subject to regulatory approvals and satellite-replacement milestones
Management projection that AWS revenue growth exceeds 40% in both 2027 and 2028, alongside a further increase in cash capital expenditures in 2027

policy_links.policy: Tariff and trade policy, which Amazon says can materially affect results, including through supply volatility in memory chips
policy_links.bottleneck: Import costs and availability of memory and other hardware used in retail goods and data-center equipment
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: Higher tariffs or scarce memory can change product costs, data-center build timing and customer demand; Amazon did not quantify a revenue amount

key_risks.risk: AI infrastructure spending has turned free cash flow negative and been funded with a large increase in long-term debt, with cash capex guided to about $220 billion in 2026 and expected to rise again in 2027
FTC and state advertising lawsuits and longer-running antitrust cases seek penalties, restitution and structural relief that could affect the ads and marketplace businesses
An ITC patent case seeks to bar imports of specified AWS AI servers, including GB200 and alleged GB300 configurations
More than $200 billion of Level 3 Anthropic preferred and convertible-note value, plus a contingent $20 billion funding facility, can swing reported earnings and future cash commitments
Tariffs and memory-chip supply are explicit swing factors in fourth-quarter guidance

notes: No going-concern language was found in the September 30, 2026 10-Q. No public equity offering, ATM or convertible issuance by Amazon was found for the last 12 months; the share-count increase is from restricted stock units, and the Globalstar deal may issue Amazon shares only if it closes in 2027. The 10-Q filing date of October 30, 2026 is taken from the EDGAR index for accession 0001018724-26-000040. A November 2026 FTC press-release URL about the advertising case returned a 404, so that case is cited only from the 10-Q. The fourth-quarter 2026 earnings date was not announced in the sources reviewed. Anthropic fair-value amounts are Level 3 management estimates. Cash of $55.8 billion, marketable securities of $58.4 billion and undrawn revolvers mean the debt increase is not treated as a solvency threat.
